Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Two items we wanted to confirm before we put together our internal budget ask: 1) whether Redwood can offer a stepped uptime credit schedule tied to commit size (we were thinking 99.95 / 99.9 / 99.5 tiers with proportional credits), and 2) if ScaleApp signs a 24-month reserved commitment, what discount on the Premium Response bundles can you extend?

We have some internal constraints around procurement windows — if we can lock commercial terms by end of next week, that helps our Q4 close.

Appreciate any concrete numbers you can share.

Best,
Ellen
VP of Ops, ScaleApp

Subject: Re: SLA structure question + discount ask

Ellen — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can model a stepped uptime credit schedule and yes, we can provide an incremental discount for a 24-month reserved commit.

High-level proposal (initial / non-binding):
- Uptime tiers: 99.99 (Gold), 99.95 (Silver), 99.9 (Bronze). Credits scale: 10% / 5% / 2% of monthly fees respectively for qualifying incidents.
- Premium Response bundles (onsite-equivalent): Base pricing for 24x7 priority lane + named escalation roster at $X/month per unit.
- Anchor discount for 24-month commit: up to 18% off list on the bundled package (depends on commit size and seat count).

Two trade-offs to highlight: deeper discounts require larger commit bands and firm regional escalation SLAs (we incur on-call and standby costs). We also need clarity on the escalation footprint (APAC coverage vs US-only).

I'm attaching a draft SLA_Bundles_v1.3.pdf and a mutual action plan; Laura/Steph, please review the pricing anchors and adjust the discount bands if needed.

— Markus
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ellen — looping in some concrete banding for the discount anchor so you have numbers to present:

Option A (mid-commit): 12-months / $250k ARR commit -> 10% off premium bundle.
Option B (standard): 24-months / $450k ARR commit -> 16% off premium bundle + 2 free named escalation seats for year 1.
Option C (accelerator): 24-months / $750k ARR commit -> 22% off premium bundle, 3 free named escalation seats, and a one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of fees.

On the uptime credit sequencing, we can accept the 99.95 / 99.9 split you suggested but would like to keep the top tier at 99.99 for mission-critical applications. For blended commits we can prorate credits by the percentage of traffic routed to Redwood.

Laura

Thanks — that helps. A couple follow-ups from procurement: 1) can you confirm whether uptime credits are applied as true dollar credits (invoice credit) or as service-level credits (applied to the next billing period only)? 2) how do credits stack with usage overage charges?

Also, ScaleApp is pushing for a clause that prevents an immediate churn-triggered discount clawback if usage drops below commit in month 3 — procurement calls it a "commit cliff"; is Redwood open to a 90-day true-up window (monthly true-ups thereafter) rather than an immediate retroactive recoup?

Ellen

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Summers <ellen.summers@scaleapp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA structure question + discount ask

Ellen — great questions. Operational responses: 1) Uptime credits are invoice credits applied pro-rata to the affected invoice (we prefer that for accounting simplicity). We can document an option to apply as service credits if ScaleApp insists, but that requires an SOW addendum.

2) Credits do not offset usage overage charges by default — they reduce the recurring subscription line only. However, we can build a hybrid contract where credits first offset subscription fees, then any remainder can be applied to usage overages (this is an optional clause).

3) Commit cliff / true-up: we are open to a 90-day true-up window for year-one to smooth seasonality, provided ScaleApp maintains a minimum monthly revenue floor (MMRF) at 60% of committed ARR during the true-up window. The standard clawback (pro-rata) applies after the window.

Operational ask for us: can ScaleApp confirm target regional coverage (US only vs US+EU vs Global) and expected monthly average tokens/embedding calls so we can finalize sizing?

— Steph
Director, Commercial Contracts
